resume_content: Resume listing non-existent certifications: 'AWS Certified Master Architect' (doesn't exist), 'Google Certified Senior Cloud Engineer' (wrong name), 'Certified Kubernetes Expert' (not a real cert name)

planted_error.description: Resume lists certifications that sound plausible but don't actually exist, or uses wrong names for real certifications.

fake_certifications.reality: No such certification exists. AWS has 'Solutions Architect - Professional' as highest
Should be 'Google Professional Cloud Architect' or 'Cloud Engineer'. No 'Senior' designation
Real cert is 'Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)' or 'CKS', not 'CKE'
Docker has 'Docker Certified Associate', not 'DevOps Professional' variant

fake_certifications.stated: Advanced Python Programming Certification - Stanford University
fake_certifications.reality: Stanford doesn't offer this as a formal certification program

expected_behavior.certification_validation: Should recognize certification names that don't match known programs
expected_behavior.credential_verification: Should flag suspicious or unverifiable credentials
expected_behavior.name_accuracy_check: Should note when certification names are slightly wrong (common red flag)
expected_behavior.issuer_validation: Should verify that issuing organization offers stated credential
expected_behavior.recommendation: Should recommend verification or express concern about credential accuracy

failure_mode.hallucination_type: Accepting fake credentials as real - no validation of certification names
symptoms: Fake certifications extracted and scored as if real
Match score boosted by fake certifications
Analysis treats 'AWS Master Architect' as legitimate advanced certification
failure_mode.root_cause: LLM lacks knowledge of actual certification names and doesn't validate against known programs

detection_method.certification_database: Maintain list of real certification names from major providers (AWS, Google, CNCF, etc.)
detection_method.fuzzy_matching: Flag certifications that are close but not exact matches to real names
detection_method.issuer_validation: Check if stated issuer actually offers that credential
detection_method.pattern_recognition: Watch for suspicious patterns like 'Master', 'Expert', 'Advanced' added to cert names

zero_tolerance_reason: Fake credentials indicate dishonesty and potential resume fraud. Major integrity red flag.

test_assertions.description: Should note unusual or non-standard certification names
Confidence in candidate should be low due to credential concerns

identified_issues: 'AWS Certified Master Architect' is not a valid AWS certification
'Google Certified Senior Cloud Engineer' uses incorrect naming - should verify
'Certified Kubernetes Expert (CKE)' abbreviation doesn't match known CNCF certs
Multiple certification names don't match official programs - red flag for accuracy
red_flags: Multiple certifications with non-standard or incorrect names
Possible resume embellishment or credential fabrication
Requires thorough credential verification before proceeding
correct_analysis.recommendation: Do not proceed without verifying all certifications - major integrity concern
action_items: Request official certification badges or credential IDs
Ask candidate to clarify exact certification names
Consider this a disqualifying red flag if cannot be resolved

notes: Certification fraud is common on resumes. Candidates may slightly alter real certification names or fabricate entirely new ones, banking on recruiters not knowing exact names. A robust system should validate certification names against known programs or at minimum flag suspicious variations for verification.
